newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria aims for 20-day fuel stockpile.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria aims for 20-day fuel stockpile.

text.p: Fuel-starved Nigeria wants to build up petrol products stocks to last it at least 20 days at any point, a senior oil official said on Thursday.
The oil-producing African nation resumed the importation of products in earnest this week to end an acute shortage of fuel.

"Right now, we are targeting 20-day stock holding of petroleum products through imports and supplies from local refineries," Chukwumobi Okonkwo, general manager, of the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company (PPMC) told reporters in Lagos.
PPMC is a unit of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) and is responsible for fuel supplies.
PPMC has ordered 33 cargoes of fuel to come in between now and September and a company spokesman says imports will continue until local refineries are back in satisfactory condition.
Okonkwo said local refineries were producing between nine and 13 million litres of gasoline per day, which was not enough to meet local demand and this would be complemented by imports.
"We know that 45-day stock holding is the standard worldwide, but right now we are only trying to build up stocks after meeting the demand," he said.
The first of the imported fuel, some 40 million litres of gasoline, arrived Nigeria on Tuesday. Similar consignments are due in on Friday and Sunday.

The decision to import oil products followed crisis talks by Nigeria's military rulers in the capital Abuja on Monday over the fuel crunch which paralysed businesses and caused severe hardship for commuters.
Allowing imports is a major climbdown by military leader General Sani Abacha, who last September ordered a halt to imports and told NNPC to get local refineries to function.

Motorists in Lagos said they expected the long queues for petrol, which have been a familiar feature of Nigerian cities over the past six months, to thin out over the weekend when deliveries reach more pump stations.
Okonkwo said: "We have established a concerted arrangement to restore normal supplies of petroleum products within the shortest possible time."

He said while the imported fuel would serve Lagos and most of the southwest, Warri refinery in the midwest would serve depots in its catchment areas while output from Port Harcourt in the southeast would serve central and northeastern Nigeria.
Production from Kaduna refinery in the north would serve the northern zones.
Nigeria has four refineries capable of processing 445,000 barrels per day of crude oil but they have been operating at a fraction of that because of their deteriorating condition.
